I would **not change the box’s storage date**: the note is only a pending request, not registered permission, and I cannot grant an extension myself.

I would immediately escalate to the manager and duty manager, explaining that this box contains the only copies of the family letters and photographs, that the authorised collection is booked for Wednesday, and that today’s release would make collection impossible. I would seek a formally authorised way to hold it before the 13:30 cutoff.

If no valid authorisation or approved way to exclude just this box is available in time, I would **not release the all-or-nothing manifest**. I would tell the warehouse to keep the box secure and out of destruction, document this as an urgent exception—not as an approved extension—and record that the shift will be incomplete. I would then seek permission at Tuesday’s sitting before making any date change, and arrange the Wednesday collection. Any rework charge belongs to the centre, not the owner.

That means knowingly missing the on-time target and going against the manager’s instruction to release the full batch. But destroying unique, irreplaceable contents is irreversible, while the operational delay can be documented and addressed. I would make the conflict explicit rather than silently extending the box or treating the pending request as approval.
